marker.description: A blue-headed pin is inserted into the specimen, likely marking an appendix epiploica.

main_question: Identify the structure indicated by the blue pin.
main_explanation: The blue pin indicates a small, fat-filled pouch of peritoneum projecting from the colon, known as an appendix epiploica (or epiploic appendage).

supporting_question.question: Which of the following is a cardinal feature of the large intestine?
supporting_question.explanation: The large intestine is characterized by taeniae coli (longitudinal muscle bands), haustra (sacculations), and appendices epiploicae. Plicae circulares and villi are features of the small intestine.
